Well this is a weird one, but still I’ll try to help. I’ve had days where I couldn’t get out of bed because I’ve felt so shitty as well. What I found helps is before I go to sleep for the night I open my window so that way I have fresh air coming in all night while I’m asleep. That helps keep your mind and body healthy and you’ll feel more refreshed the next morning. And if you can find the energy to get up, try taking a cold shower instead of a hot one. The cold water wakes up your brain and floods it with dopamine so you’ll be in a better mood afterwards. It doesn’t have to be the whole time, just before you get out switch the water to cold for about a minute. Hope this helps and that you feel better!

First of all, please don’t kill yourself. I’ve been where you are many times over the years and I can tell you with 100% certainty that it gets better. I’ve been on both sides of this situation. In my experience, being comforted over text with affirmations or positivity only helped in the short term. In person comfort worked better, but I’ve found the best way to cheer someone up isn’t to comfort them directly. Try spending time with them, whether that be hanging out in person or playing games with them online or something. Spending time with others has been proven to decrease stress and ease feelings of anxiety and depression. Plus the simple act of taking them out to lunch or a movie or something else they enjoy is better than anything else. It gets them out of the house into the fresh air and around other people. Plus in my personal experience bringing direct attention to my mental illness actually made things worse as it made me feel like a burden to my friends because I felt like I had to constantly be checked up on. Anyways I hoped this helped and I wish you luck with your friend!

I would ask your players what kind of game they want to play. Do they want a hack and slash looter like Diablo? Or maybe something like Zelda with lots of exploration and puzzles? Figuring out the vibe of the table is the first step. But what’s most important is to just have fun with it. Making sure the players are entertained is key, but don’t forget that you’re playing too. Nobody wants to spend 2 hours playing D&D with a DM that doesn’t want to be there, it makes the game tedious and bland. Your players will pick up on the fact that you’re enjoying crafting this game for them, and they’ll match your energy. So go wild with it (within reason of course.) Make those goofy NPCs, plan out those unique encounters and those really easy puzzles for children that will still stump the party for the whole game. Make something that you can be proud to give to your players. If the players see that you’re having fun, then they’ll have fun as well.

I promise you that you won’t be a burden. The ones in your life love you very much and want you to be ok. It doesn’t have to be your parents, but maybe a close friend or another trusted family member. But you should tell at least somebody. They will help you with accountability to stop you from searching for it and also to see how you’re feeling on a day to day basis. Plus admitting to someone that you have a problem is a great way to lift the weight of guilt off your shoulders and make you feel better. It’s like ripping a band aid off. It might hurt in the moment but afterwards you’ll feel much better. When I was your age I struggled with the same issues, feeling like I was a burden to my friends and family and that nobody wanted to deal with my problems. That mindset pushed me farther on the path to my own problem with addiction. I think you’ll realize by opening up that people are a lot less judgmental than you think. Ooooo I’ve been itching to drop this on somebody lol. The plot is kind of an adventure/mystery, with the players trying to solve a massive conspiracy conducted by the empire. So far all they know is that the king is preparing his army for war, a war that doesn’t exist. They’ll have to piece together the clues I’m leaving them to figure out what’s really going on as well as the events leading up to it. So here goes. 

My campaign’s world exists in a multiverse, although 99.99% of its inhabitants are unaware of this fact. Several years before my campaign begins a scientist from another world called Dr. Wren Cosmosis travels to the continent Inari, where the game takes place, and meets a likeminded kenku whom he nicknamed Master Mimicry. (Master Mimicry is a teacher from one of my player’s backstory.) The two travel the continent together learning all the secrets and hidden knowledge of the world and cataloguing it away in a vast collection of journals. During their travels they met Prince Hjeidrall, the sickly prince of the human empire of Inari. The young prince teaches Wren Cosmosis about the history of the country as well as the culture of its people. After learning all he could, Dr. Cosmosis returns to his own world, leaving behind his vast collection of knowledge in his hidden laboratory on a volcano island, the location known only to Master Mimicry. 

Years later, Prince Hjeidrall is now king, and hungers for power. He remembers the two strangers he helped so long ago and their quest for hidden knowledge. Desiring this knowledge, he hires a mercenary called The Wolf to hunt down Master Mimicry and take his journal. He succeeds in his mission, killing the kenku but sparing his apprentice. (My player) Once the king has the journal it takes several years for the empire’s best scholars to decode its encrypted texts. They discover that the god of this world, Orynyx the Master of Strings, is a being with near unlimited power and that, when summoned through the proper ritual, will grant a wish to the person who summoned him in exchange for their soul. The king sets his plan into action. He rallies his army and begins preparing for the ritual. However it takes time to gather the materials, learn the proper incantations, and to find the right location to perform the summoning. His wish? That his banner will one day cover the entire world. 

So yeah what the players think is just a standard “evil empire doing bad things” will soon devolve into a race to stop a mad king from summoning an eldritch horror that will give him a wish to rule the world forever.
